title: The 5 Largest Oceans on Earth, Ranked (#1 Beats All the Land)

scenes.text: The five oceans, ranked by size. Number one is bigger than all of Earth's land.

scenes.label: Arctic · ~12-15M km²
scenes.text: Number five: the Arctic. Roughly twelve to fifteen million square kilometers, depending on its edge, much of it frozen.

scenes.label: Southern · ~21M km²
scenes.text: Number four: the Southern Ocean. About twenty-one million square kilometers, and it wraps all the way around Antarctica.

scenes.label: Indian · ~70M km²
scenes.text: Number three: the Indian Ocean. Around seventy million square kilometers of warm water between Africa and Australia.

scenes.label: Atlantic · ~82M km²
scenes.text: Number two: the Atlantic. About eighty-two million square kilometers, roughly half the size of the Pacific.

scenes.label: Pacific · ~165M km²
scenes.text: Number one: the Pacific. Around one hundred and sixty-five million square kilometers, more than every continent put together.

description:
The five oceans of Earth, ranked by surface area.
From the Arctic to the Pacific, which covers around one hundred and sixty-five million square kilometers, more than all of Earth's land combined. Figures vary by source.
Which ocean would you sail across?
first_comment: Which ocean would you explore first? And what should we rank next?
